established_memories.guidance: When searching for an object, prioritize receptacle types that are semantically likely to contain the object (e.g., pans on stoves, food in fridges) rather than a fixed arbitrary priority (drawers > cabinets). If no semantic prior exists, use the spatial order from the initial observation as a baseline, as it may be more efficient than exhaustive type-grouping in rooms with mixed layouts. Note that semantic prioritization may increase search time if the high-probability container is empty and the target is located in a less-likely but spatially earlier or later receptacle.

established_memories.guidance: When searching for perishable food items like tomatoes in kitchens, prioritize inspecting open surfaces (countertops, shelves) before closed storage units (cabinets, drawers, fridge). This avoids the action cost of opening/closing containers. Note that if the target is not on the first few open surfaces, the fallback to closed storage may still require many steps; consider integrating spatial proximity into the open-surface traversal order if available.
